title: Synthetic Journey & SLA Calibration Playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview:

This playbook defines a standard, repeatable approach for creating, validating, and operating synthetic customer journeys used to calibrate SLAs/SLOs and drive data into QBRs. Synthetic journeys are deterministic, automated requests that emulate customer behavior across the Redwood Inference product surface (API calls, streaming, embeddings, and model switchover flows). The goal is twofold: (1) provide stable, reproducible signals for SLI measurement and drift detection, and (2) offer a lightweight smoke harness for onboarding and post-cutover verification.

Intended audience:
- Customer Success Engineers (CSEs)
- Onboarding Engineers
- SRE and Observability owners
- Product Managers running QBRs

Purpose and success criteria:
- Produce at least 6 stable synthetic journeys per enterprise tenant within the first 30 days of onboarding.
- SLIs derived from synthetic runs (latency P95, request success rate, model-consistency pass rate) should correlate with 0.8+ Pearson correlation against real-traffic SLIs across three sampled customers before being used for SLA enforcement.
- Synthetic-driven alerts should reduce false-positive operational tickets by 25% within 90 days when used as preflight checks for deployments.

Scope:
- Applies to Hosted and Dedicated deployments. Private (on-prem/VPC) deployments should adopt the same tests but may need network-specific configuration documented in the tenant's runbook.

Owners and contacts:
- Playbook owner: Maya Chen (Customer Success)
- Observability owner: Arjun Patel (Eng SRE)
- Runtime/Model owner: Dr. Priya Singh (Eng - Serving Runtime)
- Escalation contact: Support oncall (pager duty)

Prerequisites (before running a tenant's synthetic suite):
1. Tenant telemetry forwarding is enabled and validated (traces -> APM, metrics -> Prometheus/TSDB, logs -> ELK).
2. Tenant has a test API key (scoped to synthetic traffic) and a dedicated telemetry_id label for grouping.
3. Baseline artifacts checked in: canonical prompts, seed tokens for deterministic model outputs, and expected top-k outputs for consistency checks.
4. Canary traffic window scheduled (if running during a production rollout).

Synthetic journey inventory (recommended canonical suite):
1) Basic Text Generation - single-shot
   - Purpose: measure cold-start latency and first-token P95 across model variants.
   - Inputs: 3 canonical prompts (short/medium/long).
   - SLI: P95 generation latency, tokens/sec, success_rate.

2) Streaming Chat Session - streaming/long-lived connection
   - Purpose: validate chunked streaming, connection stability and knobged backpressure.
   - Inputs: 1 multi-turn conversation script (7 turns).
   - SLI: median chunk latency, connection drop rate, stream completeness.

3) Embedding Batch - high-throughput micro-batch
   - Purpose: verify batch sizing, throughput, and embedding vector stability.
   - Inputs: 128 short texts per batch.
   - SLI: throughput (vectors/sec), P99 latency per batch, cosine similarity against baseline.

4) Model Switchover & Fallback Path
   - Purpose: exercise smart routing and automatic fallback to variant models during simulated capacity constraints.
   - Inputs: request stream flagged to prefer low-cost variant.
   - SLI: success_rate_on_fallback, failover_time_ms.

5) Prefix/KV Cache Reuse Simulation
   - Purpose: validate prefix caching behavior for conversational workloads (KV-hit ratio).
   - Inputs: repeated conversation sequences to create cacheable prefixes.
   - SLI: KV_cache_hit_rate, median response delta vs uncached.

Defining SLIs -> SLOs mapping (reference):

| Synthetic test name                    | Primary SLI                        | SLO (90d lookback)                      | Alert threshold (per-tenant)             | Notes |
|----------------------------------------|------------------------------------|------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------|-------|
| Basic Text Generation                  | P95 latency (ms)                   | <= 650 ms                                | P95 > 900 ms (sustained 10m)             | Short prompts only |
| Streaming Chat Session                 | Chunk latency (ms)                 | median chunk <= 120 ms                   | median > 200 ms (5m)                     | failover to non-stream if degraded |
| Embedding Batch                        | Batch throughput (vectors/sec)     | >= 1000 vec/s                            | throughput < 500 vec/s (sustained 10m)  | tune batch size |
| Model Switchover & Fallback Path       | failover_time_ms                   | <= 300 ms                                | failover_time > 700 ms (3 tries)        | measure end-to-end |
| Prefix/KV Cache Reuse Simulation       | KV cache hit rate                  | >= 78%                                   | hit_rate < 60% (1h sustained)            | important for cost savings |
\nNote: The SLOs above are suggestions. For enterprise customers we recommend negotiating tenant-specific SLOs during the onboarding contract and recording them in the tenant runbook.

Test implementation patterns and sample commands:
- Execution harness: the recommended runner is the Redwood-synth-runner (python) located in the onboarding repo. It tags telemetry with tenant_id and synthetic=true.

Example CLI (run all canonical tests against tenant):

rdr-synth run --tenant-id tenant-abc --api-key synthetic:tenant-abc --suite canonical --interval 60s --telemetry-id tenant-abc-synth

Example minimal YAML test config (use in tenant repo):

suite: canonical
interval: 60s
tests:
  - name: basic-text-short
    type: generation
    model: rdx-base-1.2
    prompts:
      - "Summarize the following policy in one sentence: [text]"
    assertions:
      - p95_latency_ms: 650
      - success_rate: 0.995

Operational cadence and run schedules:
- Stable customers: run canonical suite every 60s, rollup hourly for dashboarding.
- Newly onboarded customers (<30 days): run extended suite every 30s and capture raw traces for the first 72 hours.
- During deploy/stability windows: increase frequency to 10s for targeted tests that validate the change (e.g., model switchover).

Alerting and routing (playbook for alerts triggered by synthetic failures):
1. Alert triage should start in the Synthetic Alert channel in Slack and create a P0/P1 incident only if real traffic SLIs also degrade or the synthetic failure is accompanied by infra-level alerts (GPU errors, network egress drops).
2. If alert is synthetic-only, follow these steps:
   a. Verify telemetry_id and that the synthetic runner tag is applied.
   b. Compare to control customers (3 control tenants with identical model profile). If only this tenant fails, escalate to CSE to validate tenant-specific configs.
   c. For repeat failures across many tenants, escalate to Eng-SRE and Mark incident as 'possible regression'.
3. Required incident fields: earliest synthetic failure timestamp, test name, recent commit hashes for runtime/model, telemetry_id, runbook link.

Triage playbook (step-by-step):
1) Confirm reproducibility:
   - Re-run the failing test from the quick-run CLI with verbose tracing: rdr-synth run --test <test-name> --tenant-id <tenant> --verbose --limit 5
   - Capture trace IDs and include in the incident.
2) Check model/variant health:
   - Inspect model-serving dashboard for kernel errors, OOMs, and recent restarts.
   - If GPU errors present, coordinate with GPU-fleet team.
3) Isolate networking/failure domain:
   - Validate that telemetry signals (request/response counts) are reaching the central TSDB.
   - For Private deployments, validate peering and NAT gateway metrics.
4) Validate configuration drift:
   - Compare tenant's pinned model version and routing policy to the onboarding baseline.
   - Check for accidental changes to caching TTLs or batch sizing.
5) Rollback/fallback decisions:
   - If a model update is the likely cause and reproduces in control tenants, execute immediate rollback to previous model version (follow model rollback runbook).
   - If the issue is degraded hardware performance, apply routing to alternate region or dedicated pool.

Reporting into QBRs and customer communications:
- Weekly digest: automated weekly summary delivered to the customer report folder (S3) showing synthetic pass/fail, trends for primary SLIs, and notable anomalies.
- QBR artifact: include a 3-month synthetic vs real-traffic correlation chart, top 3 synthetic incidents and remediation notes, and action items for improving telemetry or test fidelity.
- Post-mortem: all synthetic incidents that resulted in customer-impacting outages must have a linked postmortem in the incident tracker and an update in the tenant's onboarding playbook.

Best practices for onboarding teams (checklist):
1. Create tenant-scoped synthetic API key and label telemetry_id before provisioning.
2. Check in 3 canonical prompts and expected outputs under the tenant's repo.
3. Run extended suite for 72 hours after go-live and record baseline SLI values to the tenant runbook.
4. Publish tenant-specific SLOs in the runbook and share them during the first QBR.
5. Re-run the entire canonical suite after any runtime or model change and compare to baseline using the 'synth-delta' tool (part of rdr-synth).

Example synthetic delta command and output snippet:

rdr-synth delta --baseline tenant-abc/baseline-2024-09-12 --current tenant-abc/latest --metrics p95_latency,p99_latency,kv_hit_rate

Output (human readable):
- p95_latency: baseline 540 ms -> current 610 ms (+13%)
- kv_hit_rate: baseline 82% -> current 63% (-23%) -> ACTION: review cache TTLs

Retention and data governance:
- Synthetic logs/traces are retained for 90 days by default.
- Aggregated synthetic SLI rollups are retained for 13 months for QBR trend analysis.
- For customers with restricted data policies, mark synthetic payloads as PII-free and avoid using customer data in test prompts. Use synthetic placeholders.

Known pitfalls and mitigations:
- Pitfall: Synthetic tests are too similar and overfit the cache behavior.
  Mitigation: Rotate prompt corpus weekly and include non-cacheable prompts in 20% of runs.
- Pitfall: Synthetic-only alert fatigue.
  Mitigation: Tie synthetic alerts to a short list of high-fidelity checks (e.g., failover_time, P95 latency) and suppress noisy metrics at the alerting layer.
- Pitfall: Misaligned SLOs between commercial contract and telemetry.
  Mitigation: Always derive tenant SLOs from a calibrated 30-day synthetic baseline and get legal/finance signoff if contract-linked.

Appendix A — YAML schema (reference) for a canonical test definition:

# test definition schema (YAML)
name: basic-text-short
type: generation
model: rdx-base-1.2
prompts:
  - text: "Summarize policy: [placeholder]"
    seed: 42
assertions:
  - metric: p95_latency_ms
    max: 650
  - metric: success_rate
    min: 0.995

Appendix B — Quick escalation matrix:
- Synthetic-only failure, tenant-local: CSE -> customer success manager (CSM) -> eng-sre (if persists 30m).
- System-wide synthetic regressions: eng-sre (P0) -> runtime team -> CTO on-call if outage persists >2 hours.

Appendix C — Example dashboard widgets to include in customer QBR page:
1. Synthetic pass rate (24h / 7d / 30d)
2. P95 latency trend (synthetic vs production)
3. KV cache hit rate trend with histogram of prefix lengths
4. Top synthetic incidents and root cause tags
